text:
becky: Quick heads-up from yesterday's onboarding run: sampleapp + Node/Python batching helpers produced two different failures when SDK retries kicked in — (1) vector dim mismatch due to naive concat, (2) response shape divergence depending on path.

todd: Can you paste a tiny repro and logs?

becky: Repro is the sampleapp with mixed-length vectors (intentionally padded) + concurrent sends. Trigger flow: token refresh mid-batch -> server 502 -> SDK auto-retry. Logged outgoing chunk sequence: 
```json
{"batch_meta": {"batch_id":"b-123"}, "items": [
  {"id":"u1","vec": [0.12,0.34,0.56]},
  {"id":"u2","vec": [0.01,0.02]},
  {"id":"u3","vec": [0.9,0.8,0.7]}
]}
```
When retry/merge happened we observed assembled payloads where order and vector shapes changed: sometimes u2 moved to front and small vec lost padding. Downstream consumer assumed fixed dim and crashed on cosine calculation.

shreya: Which helper code is doing the concat? Node's FastConcat vs Python's list extend?

becky: Node uses a Buffer concat optimized path; the concat logic was merging raw Float32Array data and re-slicing by offsets that were invalidated when retries re-inserted items. Python used list-of-lists and was stable unless concurrency level > 8.

ci-bot: flakiness-detector: reproduced with randomized reorder seed=42 on CI.

todd: Oof. Any parity issues in response body shapes?

becky: Yes — when auth refresh occurred we saw two shapes returned by our rerank endpoint in the wild: flat {scores:[...]} and nested {results:{scores:[...]}}. Some SDK paths deserialize differently after retry and consumers assume one shape so mapping by index fails.

shreya: So two classes of bugs: order/dim mutation during concat and serializer parity across retry paths. Both cause index-based mapping to break.

todd: Short-term mitigation for customers: always attach stable ids and post-process mapping by id. Also validate expected dimension per id before computing similarity. Example shim: 
```
// pseudo
const mapById = (resp, ids) => {
  const scores = resp.scores || (resp.results && resp.results.scores) || [];
  return ids.reduce((acc,id,i)=> (acc[id]=scores[i] ?? null, acc), {});
}
```
But this still assumes response indices align to ids — better to ensure server returns per-item ids too.

becky: Filed DE-9977 to: (A) make helpers attach `_seq` and per-item metadata, (B) make concat deterministic and avoid low-level buffer re-slice if retries can reorder, (C) add server-side per-item `id` in responses for reliable mapping, (D) add serializer parity tests across Node/Python/Go for auth-refresh+retry. Assigned to eng-runtime + eng-ml.

devex-bot: DE-9977 created and linked to #eng-runtime, #eng-ml.

shreya: Quick patch idea: helper should not mutate original arrays; build a new reassembly array and copy references + _seq. Also canonicalize vector length or include `dim` field per item to catch padding drop.

todd: Agree. Add an integration test: simulate token expiry mid-batch, induce 502+retry, randomize batch reassembly order in test harness to catch flakiness.

becky: I'll open a small PR to the sampleapp demonstrating robust client-side mapping-by-id + dim validation. Will link DE-9977. For onboarding docs: add note "do not rely on positional alignment when retries are enabled; include stable ids and dim checks."

shreya: Can we also add a lint rule in helpers that warns if mixed vector lengths are batched without explicit padding/declared dim?

devex-bot: Noted: add lint proposal to DE-9977.

todd: Planned patch release: Node helper 0.13.1 and Python helper 0.7.4 with the deterministic reassembly and `_seq` metadata. Target this week.

becky: For anyone blocked immediately: map responses by id and assert dims; avoid in-place buffer splicing in custom code.

shreya: Thanks all. Closing this thread; follow DE-9977 for the runtime + SDK parity fixes. :thumbsup:
